deep.reconstruction:
The page is a numerical design check of a two-lens achromatic objective: a biconvex crown lens, a tiny air gap, then a biconcave flint lens. Everything is done in 7-place logarithms, with the characteristic written in the form 10+log for negatives. Two rays (colours) are followed throughout; on the next page they are labelled 'Mitth.' (middle) and 'Roth.' (red). The page computes the paraxial back focal distance for both colours. The next page repeats the job with an exact trigonometric trace of a marginal ray (columns 'Axe' and 'Rand').

DATA (top line)
- Crown indices: n_c = 1.528848 (middle), 1.519334 (red).
- Flint indices: n_f = 1.608073 (middle), 1.590263 (red).
- Radii, given as logarithms:
  - log r1 = 0.2180100, so r1 = 1.651846 (labelled 'r').
  - log r' = 0.7656313, so r2 = 5.8295.
  - log r'' = 0.5764528, so r3 = 3.770968.
  - log r''' = 0.8206316, so r4 = 6.61655.
- Signs, as implied by the formulas actually used (my inference): R1 = +r1, R2 = -r2, R3 = -r3, R4 = +r4. So the crown is biconvex and the flint biconcave.
- Thicknesses: crown d1 = 0.02, air gap g = 0.0017713, flint d2 = 0.034725.

A. CROWN, SURFACE 1 (object at infinity)
- log((n-1)/n) = 9.5389667 (middle) and 9.5337937 (red); their complements are 0.4610333 and 0.4662063.
- s1' = n r1/(n-1): log s1' = 0.2180100 + 0.4610333 = 0.6790433, so s1' = 4.775769. Red: 4.832994.
- Subtract d1 = 0.02 to get s2 = 4.755769 and 4.812994; log s2 = 0.6772207 and 0.6824154.

B. CROWN, SURFACE 2 (glass to air)
- Formula used: 1/s2' = n/s2 + (n-1)/r2 = (n-1)[n/((n-1)s2) + 1/r2].
- n/((n-1)s2) = 10^(0.4610333 - 0.6772207) = 0.6078727 (red: 0.6078423).
- 1/r2 = 0.1715413.
- log of the bracket = 9.8917682 (red: 9.8917513).
- -log(n-1) = 0.2766689 (red: 0.2845530).
- log s2' = 0.2766689 - (9.8917682 - 10) = 0.3849007, so s2' = 2.426055. Red: 2.470596.
- 9.8156356 = 9.5389667 - 9.7233311 = -log n_c (red: 9.8183467), used on the next page.
- Subtract the air gap 0.0017713 to get s3 = 2.4242837 and 2.4688247; log s3 = 0.3845834 and 0.3924902.

C. FLINT, SURFACE 3 (air to glass, concave)
- Formula used: n/s3' = 1/s3 - (n-1)/r3 = (n-1)[1/((n-1)s3) - 1/r3].
- The column marked 1/(n-1) holds -log(n_f - 1) = 0.2160442 (red: 0.2289547).
- 1/((n-1)s3) = 10^(0.2160442 - 0.3845834) = 0.6783609 (red: 0.6862217).
- 1/r3 = 0.2651839.
- log of the difference = 9.6161361 (red: 9.6243211).
- log(n/(n-1)) = 0.2063058 + 0.2160442 = 0.4223500 (red: 0.4304236).
- log s3' = 0.4223500 - 9.6161361 = 0.8062139, so s3' = 6.400500. Red: 6.398859.
- Subtract d2 = 0.034725 to get s4 = 6.365775 and 6.364134; log s4 = 0.8038513 and 0.8037394.

D. FLINT, SURFACE 4 (glass to air)
- Formula used: 1/s4' = n/s4 - (n-1)/r4 = (n-1)[n/((n-1)s4) - 1/r4].
- n/((n-1)s4) = 10^(0.4223500 - 0.8038513) = 0.4154308 (red: 0.4233351).
- 1/r4 = 0.1511362.
- log of the difference = 9.4220883 (red: 9.4348863).
- log s4' = 0.2160442 - 9.4220883, so s4' = 6.222371 (middle) and 6.223983 (red).
- These are the paraxial back focal distances, copied to the next page as 'Mitth.'/'Roth.' under 'Axe'.

E. CROSSED-OUT BLOCK
- This is a first, cancelled attempt at C–D: log n_f was used where -log(n_f - 1) belonged. It gave a flint 's3' of 2.813451/2.928101, plus 0.034725, i.e. 2.848176/2.962826.
- It was struck through and redone correctly as C–D.

F. THIN-LENS ROUGH CHECK (5-place block, lower left)
- Crown, middle colour:
  - log(1 + r1/r2) = 0.10835.
  - -log(1/r1 + 1/r2) = 0.21801 - 0.10835 = 0.10966.
  - With log(n_c - 1) = 9.72333, log f1 = 0.27667 + 0.10966 = 0.38633, so f1 ≈ 2.434.
- Crown, red colour: log(n_c - 1) = 9.71545, giving log f1 = 0.39421.
- Flint:
  - log(1 + r3/r4) = 0.19588.
  - -log(1/r3 + 1/r4) = 0.57645 - 0.19588 = 0.38057.
  - With log(n_f - 1) = 9.78396 and 9.77105: log|f2| = 0.59661 and 0.60952.
- Combination 1/F = 1/f1 - 1/|f2|, done with addition/subtraction logarithms:
  - Middle: -log(1 - f1/|f2|) = 0.41590, so log F = 0.80223 and F ≈ 6.341 (written '6,341').
  - Red: 0.40794, so log F = 0.80215.
  - The two colours agree in the thin-lens approximation (the achromatic condition).

G. START OF THE EXACT TRACE (bottom centre)
- log h = 9.2889196, so the ray height is h ≈ 0.19448.
- log sin i1 = log h - log r1 = 9.0709096, so i1 = 6°45'41.270'' ('in 6,45,41,270').
- This is the input for the trigonometric marginal-ray trace on folio 1v.
- My observation: the air gap 0.0017713 ≈ (h²/2)(1/r3 - 1/r2) ≈ 0.0017708. So the gap appears chosen so that the two lenses just touch at the rim of the aperture h.
errors: No substantive errors in the surviving computations; all recomputed values agree to within the last place.
The crossed-out block (first attempt at the flint surfaces) is wrong and was cancelled by Gauss himself. It apparently used log n_f in place of -log(n_f - 1) and gave s3' ≈ 2.813 instead of 6.4005.

Thin-lens 5-place block: -log(1 - f1/|f2|) recomputes to about 0.41580 rather than the written 0.41590 (red: 0.40786 vs 0.40794). This is a last-digit-level discrepancy in a rough check and is harmless.

results.what: Surface-by-surface paraxial ray trace (vergence/conjugate-distance formula n'/s' = n/s + (n'-n)/R with transfer through thicknesses), done in logarithms, for a crown–flint doublet in two colours, giving back focal distances 6.222371 and 6.223983
results.modern_name: Paraxial ray trace / Gaussian conjugate equation per surface
results.usually_credited_to: Standard since Huygens/Euler/Lagrange; routine in 18th–19th c. dioptrics

results.what: Thin-lens check: 1/f = (n-1)(1/R1 - 1/R2) for each lens, combination 1/F = 1/f1 + 1/f2, equality of F in two colours (achromatism)
results.modern_name: Lensmaker's equation and thin-lens achromatic doublet condition

results.what: Setting up an exact trigonometric marginal-ray trace (sin i = h/r) to compare with the paraxial (axial) focus, i.e. to assess spherical aberration and its colour variation (continued on 1v)
results.usually_credited_to: Practised by Fraunhofer, Gauss (1817 paper on achromatic double objectives) and others

results.what: Air gap chosen so that the lenses touch at the aperture rim: g ≈ (h^2/2)(1/r3 - 1/r2)

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine numerical design calculations for an achromatic doublet: paraxial trace, thin-lens achromat check and the start of an exact ray trace. Gauss's 1817 work on achromatic double objectives is well known, and the methods were standard at the time. The only interest is as working material showing his logarithmic computing practice and a specific lens prescription.

checkable.asserts: first-surface paraxial image distance n r1/(n-1) = 4.775769
crown second-surface image distance s2' = 2.426055 (biconvex lens)
flint first-surface image distance s3' = 6.4005 (middle colour)
paraxial back focal distance, middle colour = 6.222371
angle of incidence of marginal ray at height h=10^(-0.7110804) on r1 is 6°45'41.27''
air gap ≈ sag difference at rim (lenses touch at aperture edge), ~0 to 1e-6

The bottom-centre '0,2180100' is written with a correction (0,218 o100); its value is 0.2180100 (log r1).
